cards.title: Reasoning Core: 50 Procedural Generators for Completion-Supervised Reasoning Fine-Tuning
cards.why_it_matters: If you're building or evaluating post-training pipelines, this benchmarks procedural data quality in a way that directly informs dataset design decisions.
cards.summary: Reasoning Core offers 50 procedural generators across math, logic, planning, formal languages, games, and code, with semantic scorers and difficulty controls. In a 3B-parameter comparison it outperforms Procedural Warmup, Reasoning Gym, and SynLogic on DROP, LogiQA, and ARC-Challenge. Audits reveal subtle generation-rendering-scoring mismatches across all collections, flagging compact targets and calibrated difficulty as key design factors.

cards.title: Cavity-Free Quantum Interconnect Using Rydberg Neutral Atoms Hits >3×10⁵ s⁻¹ Entanglement Rate
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers tracking quantum networking hardware, this cavity-free architecture achieves entanglement rates approaching two-qubit gate speeds on current neutral-atom processors, a critical scalability threshold.
cards.summary: The proposed interconnect exploits Rydberg-state dipole-dipole interactions in ytterbium atoms to entangle stationary qubits with propagating photons without an optical cavity. Theoretical analysis shows entanglement-generation rates above 3×10⁵ s⁻¹ are achievable, approaching rates compatible with native two-qubit gates on neutral-atom processors, with inherent design flexibility for distributed quantum networks.

cards.title: Argus Agentic Runtime Hits 78% on SWE-Bench Pro with Fixed-Weight Self-Evolution via Verified State
cards.why_it_matters: A working researcher building or evaluating AI agents will want to study how Argus's verification-gated self-evolution achieves efficiency gains and recovery without any weight updates.
cards.summary: Argus uses Manager, Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer roles over durable project state, admitting memories and skills only after role-owned review. On GPT-5.5, it scores ~78% on SWE-Bench Pro vs. 59% for Direct Copilot using 1.41× tokens; after self-evolution, mature waves use 21% fewer solve-input tokens and 15% less active workflow time, with 34 verifier recoveries and 22 review-loop rescues recorded.

cards.title: OctoLong: Cross-Repository Code Contexts via AST+LSP Pipeline Boosts Long-Context LM Performance
cards.why_it_matters: For engineers training or evaluating long-context code models, the finding that replacing just 12% of standard training data with dependency-rich cross-repo contexts yields substantial gains is immediately actionable.
cards.summary: OctoLong uses an AST parser, language server, and package manager to recursively retrieve code references, generating millions-of-token dependency-rich contexts. Models from 600M to 14B parameters are mid-trained on ~50B tokens (including ~6.2B OctoLong tokens) then instruction-tuned on ~10B tokens. Replacing 12% of traditional context-extension data with OctoLong data improves long-range retrieval, state tracking, repo-level understanding, and agentic tasks versus 18 open-weight baselines.

cards.title: Constant-Depth Circuits Prepare Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall States on 156-Qubit IBM Heron
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers at the quantum ML and quantum hardware frontier, the counterintuitive result that exotic non-Abelian FQH states are cheaper to prepare than Abelian ones has direct implications for topological quantum computation strategies.
cards.summary: A systematic framework prepares 18 families of FQH states on quantum circuits with two-qubit depth independent of system size for clustered non-Abelian states, while the Abelian Laughlin state requires linear-depth sequential circuits. The parafermionic Read–Rezayi Z₃ state is held at depth 3 from 8 to 118 qubits; a 154-qubit, 104-electron Read–Rezayi Z₄ state is demonstrated. Experiments on IBM Heron recover expected fractional quasihole charges and non-Abelian e/4 quasihole braiding data.
